context: C2FO's own Oct. 27 release and Ripple's parallel release publish different historical Early Pay working-capital totals. The discrepancy must be retained without treating either figure as new XRPL capital.
decisions: Treat XLS-68 Sponsor as not active on Mainnet until canonical amendment state confirms activation; current independent roll call is 9 yes of 34 heard, 28 required, short by 19.
Track fixCleanup3_4_0 separately from Sponsor. Its current 33/34 majority and projected Nov 4 activation are conditional and may reset.

Treat SponsoredAccountCreate PR #8606 and SponsorV1_1 as a separate proposed path; no zero-balance account creation feature is live until code is accepted, released and the required amendments activate.

Model sponsorship as a shift of reserve and fee obligations from Sponsee to Sponsor. Sponsor-held XRP can be encumbered; fees remain XRP-denominated and burned. Do not assume this creates incremental spot buying without sponsor acquisition evidence.

Add future feature fields for sponsored account counts, sponsor reserve XRP, prefunded sponsorship balances, sponsored fees, XRP fee burn, sponsor concentration, sponsor identity class, sponsor exchange/OTC inflows and reserve-release events.

Keep RLUSD transfer counts, gross RLUSD volume, C2FO Early Pay historical volume and C2FO Instant Pay funded volume as separate metrics. The $525B historical Early Pay figure is not XRPL Instant Pay capital.
Record BNY custody, BNY RLUSD reserve custody, BNY Ripple Prime custody and C2FO XRPL trade-finance exploration as separate edges. None alone proves XRP buying or collateral holdings.

Record Ripple National Trust Bank final approval separately from operational status; keep Standard Custody & Trust Company as RLUSD issuer and BNY as primary reserve custodian unless new evidence changes the roles.

Treat Coinbase Q3 average USDC balances, USDC economics share, stablecoin revenue and Circle distribution costs as distinct metrics. RLUSD listing indicates multi-issuer distribution, not confirmed USDC displacement.

Do not admit sponsorship vote counts, stablecoin gross flows, company-reported market share or waitlist announcements as directional XRP price features until point-in-time data and out-of-sample tests establish predictive value.
Preserve C2FO's >$525B and Ripple's >$520B historical Early Pay statements as publisher-specific figures; do not average or silently overwrite either.
Use C2FO's own release as the primary source for its historical Early Pay metric, while retaining Ripple's parallel figure as a documented discrepancy.
Do not use either historical Early Pay figure as C2FO Instant Pay production volume, XRPL settled value, XRP demand or actual new capital deployment.

prediction_feature_contract.sponsor_concentration: share of sponsored accounts/reserve by sponsor
prediction_feature_contract.sponsor_xrp_otc_acquisitions: publicly disclosed or on-chain-identified OTC acquisition only

invariants: No current SponsoredAccountCreate or Sponsor Mainnet activation is assumed.
No C2FO Instant Pay capital is inferred from historical Early Pay volume.
No BNY XRP purchases or collateral holdings are inferred from custody announcements.
No Coinbase USDC displacement by RLUSD is assumed.
Historical Early Pay volume and C2FO Instant Pay production volume are separate variables; neither is inferred from the other.
The $525B/$520B publisher discrepancy is retained in provenance and is not averaged.

source_discrepancies.metric: Historical C2FO Early Pay working capital accessed
source_discrepancies.treatment: Preserve publisher-specific figures; no average; not Instant Pay deployment.
